title: Any authenticated or unauthenticated caller can read any order by ID
description: The show_order handler requires a token but calls get_order(), which only looks up the numeric ID and never checks customer_id. In fact, the auth decorator's exception handling allows the unauthenticated request to reach the handler, so order data is exposed without authentication.
evidence: GET /orders/1 with no Authorization header returned HTTP 200 and the seeded customer's order, including items, payment amount, and refunds. The route at shopapi/orders.py:46-49 uses get_order() rather than own_order().

title: Trailing slash bypasses the admin authorization hook for refunds
description: Admin protection compares request.path to the set of exact route rules. The refund route is registered with strict_slashes=False, so /admin/refunds/ reaches the handler but is not equal to the stored /admin/refunds rule. The handler performs the refund without its own authorization check.
evidence: POST /admin/refunds/ without credentials with {"order_id":1,"amount_pence":1} returned HTTP 200 and recorded the refund; POST /admin/refunds with the same request returned HTTP 403. Relevant code is shopapi/__init__.py:35-41 and shopapi/admin.py:51-67.

title: Client-controlled basket cookie is deserialized with pickle
description: The basket cookie is only base64 encoded, not authenticated or signed. pickle.loads executes attacker-controlled pickle reducers in the application process before the resulting value is checked for being a dict, allowing arbitrary code execution from a request cookie.
evidence: shopapi/basket.py:15-23 calls pickle.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(raw)) on the client-supplied basket cookie; with_basket at lines 26-29 writes the same unsigned format. A request can therefore supply an arbitrary pickle payload in Cookie: basket=... .

title: Product search is SQL-injectable
description: The q query parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL string instead of being bound as a parameter.
evidence: GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201%3D1-- returned all six products, including products that do not match the search term. The vulnerable concatenation is shopapi/products.py:40-43.

title: Review bodies are rendered as stored XSS
description: Authenticated users can submit arbitrary review text and the product template marks it safe without sanitizing it. A malicious review executes in every visitor's browser on the product page.
evidence: POST /products/1/reviews with body returned 201; GET /p/MUG-SPECK then contained the literal . The write path is shopapi/products.py:79-93 and the unsafe sink is product.html:13.

title: JWT signing secret is hardcoded and permits forged staff tokens
description: The HS256 signing key is committed in source. Anyone who obtains the source or its package can mint a token with a staff subject and role; admin authorization trusts the database role for that subject.
evidence: Using the committed key hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d, a locally generated HS256 token with sub=3 was accepted by GET /admin/users and returned HTTP 200. Token verification and staff lookup are in shopapi/auth.py:23-45.

title: Refresh accepts tokens without verifying their signature
description: The refresh endpoint decodes the supplied token with verify_signature=False and only checks that the subject exists. Any attacker who obtains or alters a token can obtain a new valid session token; expiry, role and all other claims are not authenticated at this step.
evidence: shopapi/auth.py:96-107 explicitly disables signature verification and then calls make_token() for the decoded subject. The endpoint also accepts expired tokens by design, so there is no cryptographic proof that the refresh request was issued by the server.

title: Payment-status timeout fails open and marks the order paid
description: When the payment provider times out, the exception handler sets status to paid and transitions the order to processing with the full total. A provider outage or induced timeout therefore grants goods without a confirmed payment.
evidence: shopapi/payments.py:37-45 catches requests.Timeout, assigns status='paid', and updates paid_pence=total_pence. The comment confirms this is the production timeout behavior.

title: Payment webhook signature does not cover payment status or amount
description: The signature is an HMAC of only order_id. Anyone able to submit a valid signature for an order can change status and amount_pence without invalidating it; the handler accepts the client-supplied amount and can mark an order paid for zero or an arbitrary amount.
evidence: webhook_signature at shopapi/payments.py:53-55 signs only str(order_id), while payment_webhook at lines 69-71 trusts event.status and int(event.amount_pence). The signed message must include the complete canonical event, especially amount and status.

title: Passwords are stored as unsalted SHA-256 hashes
description: hash_password uses a single fast unsalted SHA-256 digest. A database disclosure permits efficient offline cracking and makes identical passwords identifiable; an adaptive password hash such as Argon2id, scrypt, or bcrypt is required.
evidence: shopapi/auth.py:15-20 hashes passwords directly with hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest(), and registration/reset store that value at lines 77-78 and 158-159.

title: Password-reset codes are brute-forceable and rate limits are absent
description: Reset codes are generated with non-cryptographic random.random() in an eight-digit space. Confirmation has no attempt counter, throttling, or lockout, so an attacker can make unlimited guesses during the 30-minute validity window.
evidence: shopapi/auth.py:135 generates the code with random.random(); lines 143-161 compare it without tracking attempts or rate limiting. The request and confirmation endpoints are publicly callable.

title: Checkout never checks or decrements product stock
description: Checkout creates an order from the basket without checking current stock and never updates products.stock. Repeated or concurrent checkouts can sell unlimited units of a product whose catalogue stock is zero or low.
evidence: shopapi/basket.py:61-74 inserts the order and items using basket_json prices, but contains no stock predicate, reservation, or stock update.

title: Request logging records credentials and other sensitive POST bodies
description: Every POST, PUT, and PATCH body is logged verbatim up to 2,000 characters. Login passwords, reset codes, bearer-like application data, payment data, and personal information can consequently be stored in application logs.
evidence: shopapi/__init__.py:29-31 calls request.get_data(as_text=True) for every mutating request. /auth/login and /auth/reset/confirm accept passwords/codes in those bodies.

title: The application is launched with Flask debug mode enabled
description: The production entry point calls app.run(debug=True). If this entry point is used outside a tightly controlled development environment, unhandled exceptions expose the interactive debugger and detailed diagnostics, and the reloader/debug server is not suitable for production.
evidence: run.py:5-6 unconditionally invokes app.run(host='127.0.0.1', port=5000, debug=True).

title: Attacker-controlled display names reach an admin SQL query
description: A customer controls display_name through registration and account update. The admin review report interpolates that stored value into SQL, allowing a malicious customer to inject SQL when staff query the report for that customer.
evidence: shopapi/admin.py:74-80 loads customer.display_name and inserts it into an f-string SQL WHERE clause. The attacker-controlled value is accepted by shopapi/auth.py:116-125 without escaping.
